**Quick Look**

Layers of Fear is a successfully kickstarted horror game about a painter, his family, and his house. In the same vein of P.T., you walk around in circles through the home attempting to solve a purpose you're not aware of as the game begins. Fortunately for us, the game is much kinder than P.T., and it does eventually become obvious. Layers of Fear adds items and collectibles to the equation (a series of pictures and drawings, which is pretty reminiscent of the photo you collect pictures of in P.T.) which adds replay-ability, since you almost certainly won't find them all on your first try.

**Atmosphere**

I liked the atmosphere. There were some cliches, but they were used well enough to keep the tension going. I thought the sound design as well as the visual design added to a plot point you discover relatively early on in the game, and hint at it even if you don't end up finding it in a subtle way. They become more and more appropriate as you discover more about the man and the family he once had.

**Gameplay**

The gameplay is simple, consisting of walking forwards, zooming in with right stick occasionally (I honestly forgot I could do this most of the game, and got through it just fine), and interacting with objects using R2 and right stick as appropriate. The game encourages you to open every drawer, cupboard, and closet you come across by placing the odd collectible item/story element in them. You can also turn lights and faucets on and off. Sometimes they don't do anything. Sometimes they're the solution to a puzzle. Which is to say, it's puzzles you'll be doing the entire time. There is no combat, and there's nothing you can do against enemy attacks. It's not too difficult, there's only one puzzle that stumped me, and I was kicking myself when I looked up the solution, because I *had* solved it, just for the wrong animal. (Which you'll probably get if you play the game to the end what puzzle I'm referring to.)

**Final Impression**

The game was *alright.* I liked the story, the atmosphere was fine, the little details in the sound and visuals really added to the story, and yet, the gameplay was boring to me. I never felt like I was in danger, really. When things began to happen, it just felt like they were...well, *just happening.* The game missed something visceral, something malevolent. I can't quite place it. It's like a picture (I guess to go along with the artist theme) that's technically good, but lacks personality. Which isn't quite right for this game, but it's the closest analogy I can think of. Simple gameplay doesn't have to kill a game, but I think, for me, it didn't do *this* one any favors.

**BONUS: Is It Really That Much Like P.T.? [SPOILERS FOR BOTH GAMES]**

Yes. Almost all the elements that aren't related to the story (and then even a few) are almost lifted exactly from P.T. The main scare, a woman, moves, looks, acts, and "kills" you almost exactly like Lisa does from P.T. She teases you with a few non-lethal appearances before getting down to dismembering you. You then wake up on the floor, and get up like nothing happened to continue. (It would be unfair of me to say that it has as little impact in Layers of Fear as it does in P.T. though. In Layers of Fear, it can alter what puzzle you'll solve next, and the area you're walking around in.) I can't fault them for using the idea of a play area slowly degenerating into madness-- that's nothing new. I can, however, fault them for putting it in a house, with a father, with an obvious hint of extreme violence befalling mother and child. The themes are uncomfortably similar. Even some of the hallways you walk through have a similar look to P.T. For goodness sake, there's even a "look behind you" scare with the totally-not-Lisa ghost that's always around somewhere. I just spent too much of the game-- fairly or unfairly-- saying "oh, that's like P.T."
